questions.q: Why should Power BI connect to the Gold layer instead of Silver or Bronze?
options: Gold is pre-aggregated to a stable, stakeholder-facing shape that doesn't change on every pipeline run
Bronze and Silver are not stored as Delta tables
Power BI technically cannot query a SQL endpoint, only Gold tables
Gold tables are the only tables that contain a sale_date column
questions.explain: Bronze is raw/append-only and Silver is row-level detail that can be reshaped without warning; Gold is the stable, pre-aggregated contract meant for downstream consumers like a BI tool.

questions.q: How does Power BI's Get Data reach both Gold tables in this pipeline?
options: Through the Lakehouse SQL endpoint, selecting both gold.daily_sales_summary and gold.category_breakdown in one connection
By importing two separate CSV exports, one per table
By connecting directly to bronze.sales_raw and aggregating in Power BI itself
Through a dedicated Power BI-only copy of the Delta tables
questions.explain: Both Gold tables are exposed through the same Lakehouse SQL endpoint already used by the PySpark/SQL work in this course; Get Data selects both in the navigator.

questions.q: Why load both Gold tables into one Power BI data model instead of two separate files?
options: One model means one refresh schedule and one set of credentials, while still supporting two separate stakeholder pages
Power BI does not allow more than one table per file
Two separate files would be unable to use the same Delta tables
Because gold.category_breakdown cannot be loaded without gold.daily_sales_summary present
questions.explain: A single model simplifies maintenance (refresh, credentials, any shared logic) while each stakeholder can still get their own report page from that one model.

questions.q: Why is Import mode the right default for these two Gold tables, rather than DirectQuery?
options: Both Gold tables only change once per nightly pipeline run, so there's no value in querying live between runs
DirectQuery is not supported for Delta tables
Import mode is required whenever a table has more than one column
Gold tables are too small for DirectQuery to work
questions.explain: Since Gold only refreshes on the same nightly cadence as the pipeline, Import keeps reports fast without losing any real freshness DirectQuery would have provided.

questions.q: What is the real cost DirectQuery would introduce here, compared to Import?
options: Every slicer click or page load sends a live round-trip query to the SQL endpoint, so performance depends on that endpoint's response time
DirectQuery requires manually re-entering credentials on every report open
DirectQuery cannot read from a Lakehouse SQL endpoint at all
DirectQuery permanently deletes the source Gold tables after each query
questions.explain: DirectQuery trades Import's refresh lag for a live query on every interaction, which only pays off if the data needs to reflect changes within a day -- which this pipeline's nightly design doesn't require.
